cli.installing: kitvas: installing dependencies, this happens once after an install or update.

command.init.summary: Create the .kitvas folder in this project
command.kit.summary: Kits: kit list | show [id] | check [id] | component <Name> [id] | css [id] | build [id] | new <id> --from npm:<package>|repo:<folder> | use <id> | verify [id] | detect
command.draft.summary: Drafts: draft new <slug> [--title <text>] | list [--deleted] | show <slug> | version <slug> | delete <slug> | restore <slug> | purge <slug> | purge --all
command.layout.summary: Check a draft's layout.md against the kit and write its entry files: layout <slug>
command.context.summary: What an agent needs to write one section: context <slug> --section <id>; for a craft draft, its sketches: context <slug>
command.build.summary: Build the latest version of a draft into a page: build <slug>
command.check.summary: Check the latest version of a draft against the kit: check <slug> [--deep]
command.browser.summary: The browser kitvas checks drafts in: browser | browser install
command.studio.summary: Start the project's studio and print its address; studio status, studio stop.
command.inbox.summary: Wait for notes and requests from the studio and print them (--timeout seconds, default 30).
command.map.summary: The map of the workspace for agents: map [slug]; drafts, or one draft's sections, files and element ids.
command.guidelines.summary: The guideline book: guidelines [<id>] [--check a11y|ui|ux] [--mode auto|deep|manual] [--screen <kind>]
map.head: Draft "{slug}", version {version}, {state}, {checked}

checkHint.unknownProp: Use the props that "kitvas kit component {component}" lists.
checkHint.badValue: Use one of the listed values.
checkHint.missingProp: Add it; "kitvas kit component {component}" says what it takes.
checkHint.console: The browser reported this while showing the page; fix its cause in the draft.
checkHint.requestFailed: Put the file in src/img/ and refer to it as ../img/<file>.
checkHint.blank: Every state shows something, at least a line saying there is nothing to show.
checkHint.a11yAutocomplete: Pass the matching autocomplete value to the field, for example email, tel, given-name or postal-code.
checkHint.a11yContrastUnsure: Check this text by eye over its background. If it is hard to read, put it on a solid surface token or use a stronger text token.
checkHint.a11yControlContrast: Give the control a border or fill of at least {min}:1 against what is around it, using a border or surface token. Do not hide the control.
checkHint.a11yErrorText: Show a message under the field and link it with aria-describedby or aria-errormessage. Use the kit's error or helper text prop when it has one.
checkHint.a11yFocusContrast: Make the focus ring at least {min}:1 against what is next to it, with a stronger colour token. Do not remove the ring.
checkHint.a11yFocusHidden: Keep the focused element clear of the fixed or sticky bar: give the page scroll padding for the bar, or make the bar smaller.
checkHint.a11yFocusOrder: Put the elements in the source in the order people read them, and do not use tabindex above 0 or reversed order on focusable elements.
checkHint.a11yFocusVisible: Add a visible focus style with :focus-visible, such as an outline from a colour token. Do not set outline to none.
checkHint.a11yIconContrast: Colour the icon with a stronger text or icon token so it reaches {min}:1 against its background, and keep the button's accessible name.
checkHint.a11yReflow: Let the content wrap or stack at {width}px: use flexible widths, min-width of 0, and wrap or scroll tables and code inside their own box.
checkHint.a11yTextSpacing: Do not fix the height or width of text boxes. Let them grow with their text, and avoid overflow hidden on text.
checkHint.uiCenteredText: Align the text to the start. Keep centring for short items such as a heading or a single line.
checkHint.uiHeadingLineHeight: Tighten the heading's line height to about 1.2; it is {ratio} now.
checkHint.uiHeadingScale: Step headings clearly apart, and make the largest one clearly bigger than the body text. This one is {size}px, a ratio of {ratio} (body is {body}px).
checkHint.uiJustifiedText: Use text-align: start. Full justification leaves uneven gaps between words.
checkHint.uiLineHeight: Set a line height of about 1.4 to 1.6 on body text; it is {ratio} now. Use the kit's line-height token.
checkHint.uiLineLength: Limit the width of the text block to about 70ch with max-width; its longest line holds about {longest} characters.
checkHint.uiTextSize: Use the kit's body or small text size so text on a phone is at least 14px; this text is {size}px.
checkHint.uiTypeSizes: Reduce the page to a few sizes from the kit's type scale. It uses {count}: {sizes}px.
checkHint.uiTypeWeights: Use two or three weights, such as regular for text and one heavier weight for headings and emphasis. The page uses {count}: {weights}.
checkHint.uiCardSizes: The cards differ by {diff} px in height. Let the row stretch them to one height (align-items: stretch, or a grid) or give them the same content shape.
checkHint.uiClippedText: Let the box grow with its text, or let the text wrap. If the cut is meant, add an ellipsis or a line clamp so it shows.
checkHint.uiEdgeGap: The text is {gap} px from the edge. Add side padding from the kit's spacing tokens so it sits clear of the screen edge.
checkHint.uiFlatHierarchy: Give the page one clearly larger heading, then body text and small print, using the kit's type tokens or the Heading and Text props.
checkHint.uiHeadingGap: Move the heading closer to its own content ({below} px now) than the group is to the one above ({above} px now). Use a smaller spacing token under the heading and a larger one above the group.
checkHint.uiHueCount: The page uses {count} hues. Keep one brand colour, one accent and neutrals, from the kit's colour tokens.
checkHint.uiImageDistorted: The image is stretched by {percent} percent. Set object-fit: cover or contain, or give the box the image's own ratio with aspect-ratio.
checkHint.uiManyLarge: Keep at most two large texts per section on the first screen. Make the others body size or use a smaller step of the kit's type tokens.
checkHint.uiNestedFrame: Drop the border, shadow or fill from the inner box, or from the outer one. Separate inner parts with spacing or a divider instead of another card.
checkHint.uiOrphanCard: The last row has one card while earlier rows have {perRow}. Change the card count, or let the grid fill the row (auto-fit columns, or span the last card).
checkHint.uiPageOverflow: This element reaches {over} px past the screen. Give it max-width: 100% and let its content wrap, or put a wide table or code block in its own scroller.
checkHint.uiPlaceholderMedia: Put real images, icons or illustrations in these boxes, or remove them. Use the kit's Image or Avatar component where it has one.
checkHint.uiShadowCount: The page uses {count} different shadows. Pick the kit's shadow tokens and keep to its few elevation levels.
checkHint.uiStickyChrome: Fixed bars take {percent} percent of the screen height. Keep them slim, or make one of them scroll with the page.
checkHint.uiStrayEdge: This block starts {off} px from a column that other blocks share (x = {column}). Use the same padding and spacing tokens so the edges line up.
checkHint.uiTripleFrame: Keep one cue. Use a border for a flat card, or a shadow for a raised one, and let the fill go if it adds nothing.
checkHint.uiWireframe: Replace the placeholder boxes and copy with real content, and give the page more than one size and weight of text.
checkHint.uxBrokenAnchor: Give the target the id "{target}", or point the link at an element that exists.
checkHint.uxErrorWording: Say what is wrong and how to fix it in a short sentence, for example "Enter an email address in the format name@example.com".
checkHint.uxFieldCount: Cut the form to {max} fields or fewer: drop what can be asked later, or fill it in for the person.
checkHint.uxFieldset: Wrap the options in the kit's group or fieldset component and give it a legend that names the question.
checkHint.uxInputType: Use the type "{suggest}" for this field, so the right keyboard and checks apply.
checkHint.uxKeepsInput: Keep what the person typed when the error shows: pass the same value to the field in this state.
checkHint.uxLabelPosition: Put the label above the field, not beside it.
checkHint.uxRequiredMarks: Mark only one kind: either the required fields or the optional ones, the same way in every field of the form.
checkHint.uxSingleColumn: Stack the fields in one column on a narrow screen. Short related pairs, such as day and month, may share a row.
checkHint.uxSubmit: Add a button that submits the form, named for what it does.
checkHint.uxVisibleLabel: Give the field a label that stays on screen, using the kit's label or field prop. A placeholder may only add an example.
checkHint.uxButtonText: Name the button for its outcome, for example "Save changes" or "Delete order".
checkHint.uxCurrentPage: Set the current prop or aria-current="page" on the link of this page; the navigation has {links} links.
checkHint.uxDangerPrimary: Make the safe choice the primary one and the destructive action a secondary or warning button.
checkHint.uxEmptyNextStep: Add a sentence that says what goes here and a button or link for the first step.
checkHint.uxEmptyRegion: Show a short text or a next step where the content would be, so the blank is not read as broken.
checkHint.uxErrorRecovery: Add a button or link in the main area, such as retry or back, next to the message.
checkHint.uxHiddenNav: Show the main links in the bar on wide screens and keep the menu button for narrow ones.
checkHint.uxLinkText: Put the destination in the link text, for example "Read the pricing guide".
checkHint.uxLoadingIndicator: Mark the area with aria-busy, add a status or progressbar role, or use a kit feedback component such as a spinner or skeleton.
checkHint.uxLoadingSaysEmpty: Show a loading indicator or a skeleton while loading, and keep the empty message for the empty state.
checkHint.uxOnePrimary: Keep one filled primary action and make the others outline, plain or ghost variants.
checkHint.uxPlaceholderText: Replace it with the real text.
checkHint.uxSameTextLinks: Give each link its own text that tells its destination apart.
checkHint.uxStateShift: Keep it in the same place in every state; it moved by {dx} px across and {dy} px down.
checkHint.uiImageSize: Give the image a width and a height, or an aspect ratio in its style, so the page does not jump when it loads.
checkHint.uiTransitionAll: List the properties that change, for example opacity and transform, instead of all.
checkHint.uxAutofocus: Remove autoFocus, or move focus only after the person acts, so a screen reader and a phone keyboard are not surprised.
checkHint.uxPasteBlocked: Remove the handler that stops pasting, so password managers and pasted codes keep working.
checkHint.a11yContrastOnImage: Sampled from the pixels, its contrast is {ratio}:1 where {min}:1 is needed. Put the text on a solid surface token, add a scrim behind it, or use a text colour token that stands out from the picture.
checkHint.a11yMotion: Stop or calm the animation or video under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, or put a visible pause or stop button next to it.
checkHint.a11yOrientation: Held sideways it shows {landscape} characters of text, upright {portrait}. Remove media queries on orientation that hide content or rotate html or body, and let the layout reflow to the wider screen instead.
checkHint.uiLongNumber: Give the number room: let the cell or badge widen or wrap instead of holding a fixed width, and keep its spacing on the kit's tokens. Prices, totals and counts grow with real data.
checkHint.uiLongText: Let the text wrap and its box grow: drop the fixed width or height, let flex rows wrap or shrink their items, and size with the kit's spacing tokens. Real names and translations are often much longer.

guideline.a11yAutocomplete.rule: A field about the person, such as name, email, phone, address or card, names its purpose with autocomplete.
guideline.a11yAutocomplete.why: Browsers and assistive tools can fill and label such fields when they know their purpose. That helps people who find typing hard.
guideline.a11yContrastUnsure.rule: Text over an image, gradient or overlay is checked by eye when a tool cannot measure its contrast.
guideline.a11yContrastUnsure.why: Text needs enough contrast to be read, but a tool cannot always tell what is behind it. A person looks at those places.
guideline.a11yControlContrast.rule: The border or fill of an input, select, checkbox, radio or switch has at least 3:1 contrast with what is around it.
guideline.a11yControlContrast.why: People need to see where a control is. A visible label helps, so a control with one is only a review.
guideline.a11yErrorText.rule: A field in an error state has error text linked to it with aria-describedby or aria-errormessage.
guideline.a11yErrorText.why: An error shown only by colour or an invalid flag tells screen reader users nothing. The text says what went wrong.
guideline.a11yFocusContrast.rule: A custom focus ring has at least 3:1 contrast with what is next to it.
guideline.a11yFocusContrast.why: A ring that blends in cannot be followed by keyboard users. The browser's own ring is left alone.
guideline.a11yFocusHidden.rule: A fixed or sticky element does not cover the element that has focus.
guideline.a11yFocusHidden.why: Keyboard users lose their place when focus moves under a bar. Fully covered is wrong, partly covered is for a person to judge.
guideline.a11yFocusOrder.rule: Focus moves through a column from top to bottom, never back up.
guideline.a11yFocusOrder.why: A jump back up the page is a sign of a source order that differs from the visual one. This is a kitvas heuristic, so a person decides.
guideline.a11yFocusVisible.rule: Every element that takes keyboard focus shows that it has it.
guideline.a11yFocusVisible.why: Without a visible change a keyboard user cannot tell where they are on the page.
guideline.a11yIconContrast.rule: An icon that is the only content of a button or link has at least 3:1 contrast with its background.
guideline.a11yIconContrast.why: With no text beside it, the icon is the whole control, so it must be easy to see.
guideline.a11yReflow.rule: At 320 px wide the page does not scroll sideways, apart from tables, code and media.
guideline.a11yReflow.why: People who zoom in or use a small screen should not have to scroll in two directions to read.
guideline.a11yTextSpacing.rule: Text stays whole and apart from its neighbours when line, letter and word spacing are widened.
guideline.a11yTextSpacing.why: Some readers set wider spacing for themselves. Boxes with a fixed size cut the text off or pile it up.
guideline.uiCenteredText.rule: Do not centre blocks of text of three lines or more.
guideline.uiCenteredText.why: Centred lines start at a different place each time, so the eye has to search for the next line. It works for short items, not for paragraphs.
guideline.uiHeadingLineHeight.rule: Wrapped headings keep a line height between 1.0 and 1.35.
guideline.uiHeadingLineHeight.why: Large text with body-text spacing falls apart into separate lines. Tight spacing keeps a heading reading as one unit.
guideline.uiHeadingScale.rule: Heading sizes step apart by at least 1.1 times, and the top heading is at least 1.5 times the body size.
guideline.uiHeadingScale.why: Levels that look the same do not show the structure of the page. The numbers are kitvas starting values, in line with common type scales.
guideline.uiJustifiedText.why: Justification stretches the gaps between words unevenly, which makes reading harder for many people, especially with dyslexia.
guideline.uiLineHeight.rule: Body text of three lines or more has a line height of 1.3 to 1.8 times its size.
guideline.uiLineHeight.why: The sources recommend about 1.2 to 1.5; the band is wider so only clear misses are reported. Headings are checked by their own rule.
guideline.uiLineLength.rule: A paragraph holds at most 80 characters per line; 45 to 90 is the comfortable band.
guideline.uiLineLength.why: Very long lines make it hard to find the start of the next one. WCAG sets 80 as the limit at the enhanced level.
guideline.uiTextSize.rule: On a phone, paragraphs are at least 14px and no text is under 12px.
guideline.uiTextSize.why: Guidance for body text is 14 to 16px. The 12px floor for any text is a kitvas starting value.
guideline.uiTypeSizes.rule: A page uses at most five font sizes.
guideline.uiTypeSizes.why: Each extra size weakens the hierarchy. Nielsen Norman Group suggests three; five is a looser starting value. A size counts only when it holds 2% of the text.
guideline.uiTypeWeights.rule: A page uses two or three font weights, not one and not more than three.
guideline.uiTypeWeights.why: One weight leaves nothing to separate headings from text, and many weights look noisy. These are kitvas starting values.
guideline.uiCardSizes.rule: Cards in one row should have the same height.
guideline.uiCardSizes.why: Uneven cards make a row look broken and hide which edges belong together. A taller card also pulls the eye away from its neighbours.
guideline.uiClippedText.rule: Text must never be cut off by its box.
guideline.uiClippedText.why: Hidden words cannot be read, and enlarging the text makes it worse. A deliberate cut needs an ellipsis or a clamp so the reader knows there is more.
guideline.uiEdgeGap.rule: Keep text at least 16 px from the screen edge on a phone.
guideline.uiEdgeGap.why: Text that touches the edge is hard to read and looks unfinished. A small margin keeps lines clear of the bezel and of the thumb.
guideline.uiFlatHierarchy.rule: Use more than one size and weight of text so the page has an order.
guideline.uiFlatHierarchy.why: When everything looks the same, nothing leads the eye. A visible hierarchy tells a reader what to read first.
guideline.uiHeadingGap.rule: A heading belongs to the content under it, so put it closer to that content than to the group above.
guideline.uiHeadingGap.why: Things that sit close together read as one group. A heading floating midway between two groups could belong to either.
guideline.uiHueCount.rule: Use about two main hues and two supporting ones, plus neutrals.
guideline.uiHueCount.why: Many hues compete for attention and blur the meaning of colour. A small palette keeps emphasis where you put it.
guideline.uiImageDistorted.rule: Show an image at its own proportions, or crop it with object-fit.
guideline.uiImageDistorted.why: A stretched image looks cheap and can mislead, as faces and logos change shape. Cropping keeps the picture true.
guideline.uiManyLarge.rule: Keep at most two large elements in one section on the first screen.
guideline.uiManyLarge.why: Large elements compete, and a reader cannot tell which one matters. Two at most keeps a clear lead.
guideline.uiNestedFrame.rule: Do not put a card inside a card.
guideline.uiNestedFrame.why: Each frame says that what is inside belongs together. Frames inside frames add noise and shrink the room for content. A tinted full-width band is fine, as it is a background, not a card.
guideline.uiOrphanCard.rule: Avoid a card grid whose last row holds a single card.
guideline.uiOrphanCard.why: A lone card leaves a hole beside it and looks like something went missing. Balance the count or let the last card span the row.
guideline.uiPageOverflow.rule: The page must not scroll sideways.
guideline.uiPageOverflow.why: Content wider than the screen forces two-way scrolling and breaks reflow for people who zoom or use small screens. Wide tables and code belong in their own scroller.
guideline.uiPlaceholderMedia.rule: Do not leave plain grey boxes where images belong.
guideline.uiPlaceholderMedia.why: Empty boxes make a design look unfinished. Show the real picture, or leave the space out.
guideline.uiShadowCount.rule: Use at most four different shadows on a page.
guideline.uiShadowCount.why: Each shadow stands for a level of height. Too many levels blur the idea of what sits above what.
guideline.uiStickyChrome.rule: Fixed and sticky bars should take no more than a fifth of the screen height.
guideline.uiStickyChrome.why: Research on sticky headers finds a content-to-chrome ratio of about 13 to 1 reasonable and 2 to 1 excessive. On a phone, fixed bars eat the room the content needs.
guideline.uiStrayEdge.rule: Line up left edges: a block a few pixels off its column looks like a mistake.
guideline.uiStrayEdge.why: A shared edge makes order that the eye notices. A near miss reads as sloppy, and one pixel is invisible, so only larger offsets count.
guideline.uiTripleFrame.rule: Mark a box with one cue, not a border, a shadow and a fill together.
guideline.uiTripleFrame.why: A flat card takes a border, a raised one takes a shadow. Stacking all cues is heavy and does not say more.
guideline.uiWireframe.rule: A finished page should not look like a wireframe.
guideline.uiWireframe.why: Placeholder boxes, template words and one flat type style together say the page is still a sketch. Three of these four signs are enough to flag it.
guideline.uxBrokenAnchor.rule: A link to a place on the page must point at an id that exists.
guideline.uxBrokenAnchor.why: An error summary lists links that take the person to each field. A link to a missing id does nothing, so the person cannot find the error.
guideline.uxErrorWording.rule: An error text says what is wrong and how to fix it, in more than one word.
guideline.uxErrorWording.why: A bare "Invalid" or "Required" tells the person nothing to act on. Sources agree that a message names the problem and suggests the fix. The word list and the minimum length are kitvas's own.
guideline.uxFieldCount.rule: A checkout or sign-up form asks for no more than 8 fields.
guideline.uxFieldCount.why: Every extra field costs completions. Baymard found an average of 11.3 fields in checkout forms and sets 8 as the target.
guideline.uxFieldset.rule: Radio buttons and checkboxes that answer one question sit in a group with a legend.
guideline.uxFieldset.why: The legend is the question; without it a screen reader hears only the single options and not what they answer.
guideline.uxInputType.rule: A field uses the input type that matches what it asks for.
guideline.uxInputType.why: Email, phone and URL types bring the right keyboard on a phone. The number type suits quantities but not codes, phone numbers or postcodes.
guideline.uxKeepsInput.rule: An error never clears what the person typed.
guideline.uxKeepsInput.why: Typing a value again after a mistake is wasted work and an invitation to give up. Password fields are the exception.
guideline.uxLabelPosition.rule: On a narrow screen the label sits above its field.
guideline.uxLabelPosition.why: A label beside the field leaves too little room on a phone, and labels above are read fastest. The sources put labels on top.
guideline.uxRequiredMarks.rule: Mark required or optional fields in one consistent way within a form.
guideline.uxRequiredMarks.why: The sources disagree on which kind to mark, so kitvas checks only that a form does not mix the two or mark some fields and miss others.
guideline.uxSingleColumn.rule: A narrow form is one column of fields.
guideline.uxSingleColumn.why: One column gives a single path down the form. Two fields on a row are read out of order and get cramped on a phone.
guideline.uxSubmit.rule: A form with fields has a button that submits it.
guideline.uxSubmit.why: Without a submit button the form cannot be sent. This is a heuristic: a button outside the form element is not seen.
guideline.uxVisibleLabel.rule: Every field has a label that stays visible.
guideline.uxVisibleLabel.why: A placeholder vanishes as soon as the person types, and a label that is only hidden or aria text cannot be read at a glance. A search box with a hidden label is a common and accepted exception.
guideline.uxButtonText.rule: A button is named for what it does.
guideline.uxButtonText.why: Words like OK or Submit force people to read around the button to learn what happens.
guideline.uxCurrentPage.rule: A navigation marks the page the person is on.
guideline.uxCurrentPage.why: People need to see where they are in the site; without a mark the navigation gives no status.
guideline.uxDangerPrimary.rule: A destructive action is not the main call to action.
guideline.uxDangerPrimary.why: A prominent delete button invites mistakes; destructive actions need a calmer look or a confirmation step.
guideline.uxEmptyNextStep.rule: An empty state explains what belongs there and offers a next step.
guideline.uxEmptyNextStep.why: People who meet a blank list need to know why it is blank and what to do next.
guideline.uxEmptyRegion.rule: A region that is empty in a state must say so, not stay blank.
guideline.uxEmptyRegion.why: A blank area leaves people unsure whether it is empty, still loading or broken.
guideline.uxErrorRecovery.rule: An error state gives a way to recover.
guideline.uxErrorRecovery.why: People who hit an error need a clear step to recover, or the screen is a dead end.
guideline.uxHiddenNav.rule: On a desktop width the main navigation is visible.
guideline.uxHiddenNav.why: On desktop, hidden navigation was used in 27% of cases against 48 to 50% for visible navigation, and tasks took at least 39% longer.
guideline.uxLinkText.rule: A link text describes where it goes.
guideline.uxLinkText.why: Vague link text is useless when links are read out of context, in a list or by a screen reader.
guideline.uxLoadingIndicator.rule: A loading state shows that the system is working.
guideline.uxLoadingIndicator.why: After about a second people need a signal that the system is busy; a longer wait needs a spinner, a skeleton or a progress bar.
guideline.uxLoadingSaysEmpty.rule: A loading state never says that nothing was found.
guideline.uxLoadingSaysEmpty.why: Telling people there are no results before they arrive makes them leave or retry for nothing.
guideline.uxOnePrimary.rule: A screen section has one primary action.
guideline.uxOnePrimary.why: Two equally loud buttons make people stop and decide which one matters most.
guideline.uxPlaceholderText.rule: No placeholder copy is left in the page.
guideline.uxPlaceholderText.why: Lorem ipsum, TODO and template words such as Title or Label show a draft that is not finished.
guideline.uxSameTextLinks.rule: Links with the same text lead to the same place.
guideline.uxSameTextLinks.why: People expect equal link text to mean equal destination, and cannot tell such links apart.
guideline.uxStateShift.rule: The header, navigation and footer stay put when the state changes.
guideline.uxStateShift.why: Chrome that jumps between states looks like a layout bug and makes people lose their place.
guideline.a11yDragAlternative.rule: Anything done by dragging can also be done with a click, a tap or a key.
guideline.a11yDragAlternative.why: People who cannot hold and move a pointer still need to reorder, move or resize things. Offer buttons or menu items next to the drag.
guideline.a11yRedundantEntry.rule: Do not ask for the same information twice in one flow; fill it in or let the person pick it.
guideline.a11yRedundantEntry.why: Retyping costs effort and causes mistakes, most of all for people with memory or motor difficulties. Show what was entered earlier and let them reuse it.
guideline.uiBrandVisible.rule: The brand is visible on the first screen: its name or mark, its colour and its voice.
guideline.uiBrandVisible.why: A page that could belong to any product feels unfinished. Check that the screen looks like this product and not a template.
guideline.uiFewSizes.rule: The page uses few type sizes and at most two large elements.
guideline.uiFewSizes.why: Many sizes and many big items compete for attention, so nothing leads. A short scale keeps the order clear.
guideline.uiGroundColour.rule: The page has a ground colour or layered surfaces, not only white and grey boxes.
guideline.uiGroundColour.why: A surface behind the content gives the page depth and a mood. Boxes on a plain background look flat and generic. This is a judgement kitvas cannot measure.
guideline.uiImageSize.rule: Images carry their size, as a width and height or an aspect ratio.
guideline.uiImageSize.why: The browser can then reserve the space before the image loads, so the page does not shift while people read.
guideline.uiMobileText.rule: Body text on a phone is at least 16 px.
guideline.uiMobileText.why: Smaller text is hard to read on a small screen and often makes the browser zoom on focus. Sixteen pixels is a safe floor.
guideline.uiOneBoundary.rule: A group is set apart by one cue: a border, a shadow, a background or space, not several.
guideline.uiOneBoundary.why: One clear boundary shows what belongs together. Stacking cues adds noise without adding meaning.
guideline.uiRealCopy.rule: The text is real product copy, not filler or generic marketing words.
guideline.uiRealCopy.why: Placeholder wording hides layout problems and makes the screen untestable. Real text shows real lengths and real tone.
guideline.uiRealMedia.rule: Images show real content, not grey boxes or stock fillers.
guideline.uiRealMedia.why: Empty media blocks make a prototype hard to judge. A real picture shows how the layout holds up with real colour and shape.
guideline.uiSquint.rule: When the page is blurred, a first and a second level still stand out.
guideline.uiSquint.why: If everything blurs into one grey mass, people have no entry point. A clear first and second tier tells the eye where to start.
guideline.uiThumbReach.rule: On a phone, the main actions are large and spaced out so a thumb hits them easily.
guideline.uiThumbReach.why: Small or crowded targets cause missed taps. Large targets near where the thumb rests are faster to reach.
guideline.uiTransitionAll.rule: A transition names the properties it animates, never all.
guideline.uiTransitionAll.why: Animating all properties can move things that were not meant to move and costs more to draw. Naming them keeps motion intended.
guideline.uxAutofocus.rule: Nothing grabs focus by itself when the page opens.
guideline.uxAutofocus.why: Automatic focus can scroll the page, open the phone keyboard and skip what a screen reader would read first. Let the person choose where to start.
guideline.uxConfirmDestructive.rule: Before something is destroyed, name the item and the result, label the buttons with outcomes, and offer undo where you can.
guideline.uxConfirmDestructive.why: Yes and No buttons are easy to press without reading. A clear outcome and a way back prevent loss without nagging for every action.
guideline.uxErrorSaysFix.rule: An error message says what to change, in plain words, next to the field.
guideline.uxErrorSaysFix.why: People fix a problem faster when they are told how. A bare Invalid leaves them guessing.
guideline.uxFrontLoad.rule: Headings, links and sentences start with the words that matter most.
guideline.uxFrontLoad.why: People scan the first words of each line. Key words up front let them decide quickly without reading it all.
guideline.uxGuestCheckout.rule: Checkout lets a new customer pay without creating an account first.
guideline.uxGuestCheckout.why: Forced sign-up adds a step at the moment of purchase and makes some people leave. This is a starting value for judgement, not a sourced figure.
guideline.uxHeadingsSpecific.rule: Headings say what is in the section, not a generic label.
guideline.uxHeadingsSpecific.why: A specific heading lets people skim and find what they came for. Words like Overview or Details tell them nothing.
guideline.uxOneQuestion.rule: In a long flow, each step asks one question.
guideline.uxOneQuestion.why: One question per step keeps people focused and makes errors easy to place. It also fits small screens.
guideline.uxPasteBlocked.why: Blocking paste breaks password managers and makes people retype codes. For sign-in it can fail the accessible authentication requirement.
guideline.uxSuccessFeedback.rule: After an action, the screen shows that it worked.
guideline.uxSuccessFeedback.why: People should always know the state of the system. A saved or sent message, or a visible change, ends the doubt.
guideline.uxToggleImmediate.rule: A toggle takes effect at once; a checkbox waits for the form to be submitted.
guideline.uxToggleImmediate.why: People expect a switch to act like a light switch. Using it as a deferred choice leaves them unsure whether it applied.
guideline.uxValidateLate.rule: A field shows an error only after the person leaves it, and the error clears as soon as it is fixed.
guideline.uxValidateLate.why: An error shown while someone is still typing is premature and feels like scolding. An error that stays after the fix feels broken.
guideline.a11yContrastOnImage.rule: Text over a photo or gradient keeps the contrast text needs on a flat colour: 4.5:1, or 3:1 for large text.
guideline.a11yContrastOnImage.why: A picture changes from spot to spot, so text that reads well on one part can disappear on another.
guideline.a11yMotion.rule: Motion that starts on its own and goes on for more than a few seconds can be paused, and stops when the person asks for reduced motion.
guideline.a11yMotion.why: Moving content pulls the eye away from reading and can make some people feel ill; a pause control or the reduced motion setting gives them the choice.
guideline.a11yOrientation.rule: The page works upright and sideways and does not lock itself to one orientation.
guideline.a11yOrientation.why: Some people have their device mounted in one position and cannot turn it, so content that hides or turns in the other orientation is lost to them.
guideline.uiLongNumber.rule: Prices, totals and counts still fit when the number gets long.
guideline.uiLongNumber.why: Real numbers grow with the data, the currency and the locale, and a total that is cut off misleads people.
guideline.uiLongText.rule: Short texts such as labels, names and button captions still fit when they get much longer.
guideline.uiLongText.why: Real names, user input and translations are often far longer than sample copy, and a box that cuts them off or overflows hides what people need to read.

checkRule.uiNoViewport: The original has no viewport meta tag, so a phone shows it zoomed out.

guideline.uiNoViewport.rule: A page must set a viewport meta tag so it fits the screen width.
guideline.uiNoViewport.why: Without it a phone lays the page out on a wide canvas and shrinks it, so text is tiny and the content does not reflow to the screen.
guideline.uxBeforeProblems.rule: A rework must fix the problems the original had.
guideline.uxBeforeProblems.why: A rework that keeps every old problem changed the look and left the page as hard to use as it was. A rule that fires as often as before is reported for review.
guideline.uxProtected.rule: A rework keeps every protected item, in every version.
guideline.uxProtected.why: The person confirmed these texts, prices, fields and brand marks as the part of the page that must not change. A version that drops one changes the product, not only its look.

guideline.uiIconColour.rule: An icon paints with currentColor only; none and transparent are fine.
guideline.uiIconColour.why: A fixed colour does not follow the text colour, the theme or a dark mode, and can vanish on a ground of the same colour.
guideline.uiIconGrid.rule: A new icon uses the same viewBox as the kit's icons.
guideline.uiIconGrid.why: Icons drawn on one grid share their padding, optical size and pixel snapping. An icon on another grid looks larger, smaller or blurred next to them.
guideline.uiIconSmall.rule: At 16 px, no part of an icon is thinner than one device pixel.
guideline.uiIconSmall.why: A line under one pixel is drawn as a pale blur, so a small icon loses its shape exactly where icons are used most: in buttons, lists and fields.
guideline.uiIconStroke.rule: A new icon keeps the stroke width of the kit's icons.
guideline.uiIconStroke.why: A heavier or lighter line makes one icon stand out or fade among the others, and the set stops reading as one family.
guideline.uiLogoContrast.rule: A logo keeps at least 3:1 against both a light and a dark ground, by itself or through its tones.
guideline.uiLogoContrast.why: A graphic people need to recognise must stand out from what is behind it. A mark that fades on white or on black disappears in half the places it is used.
guideline.uiLogoMono.rule: A logo has a variant in one colour.
guideline.uiLogoMono.why: Favicons, stamps, dark headers and printed pages often allow one colour only, and a logo without such a variant gets recoloured by hand.
guideline.uiLogoSmall.rule: A logo stays legible at 32 px, with no part thinner than one device pixel.
guideline.uiLogoSmall.why: Logos are shown tiny in tabs, favicons and lists. Fine lines and small lettering blur away there, and the mark becomes a blot.
guideline.editLockedChanged.rule: A locked element keeps the source it was locked with.
guideline.editLockedChanged.why: The person locked it to say this part is done. A change by Claude or another editor is shown to them, never reverted on its own, so they decide.

studio.guide.title: Guide
studio.guide.lead: kitvas builds UI prototypes from your project's own design system, checks them, and shows them in a local studio where you can edit them.
studio.guide.how.title: How it works
studio.guide.how.teach: Teach kitvas your design system, or go on with Base, the built-in kit.
studio.guide.how.ask: Ask Claude for a screen. It plans the sections and builds them from the kit.
studio.guide.how.read: Read the checks. kitvas type-checks the draft, applies the kit's rules, and opens the page in a real browser at 390 and 1280 px.
studio.guide.how.change: Change it in the editor, or give feedback in chat or as a note in the studio. Each round makes a new version.
studio.guide.skills.title: Start in Claude Code
studio.guide.skills.lead: In your project folder, in Claude Code, type one of these.
studio.guide.checks.title: Checks
studio.guide.checks.what: kitvas check builds a draft and checks it: the build, types, the kit's rules, and the page in a browser at 390 and 1280 px, in every state. The browser checks cover accessibility, the look, the flow and errors at runtime.
studio.guide.checks.findings: Every finding has a place, a message and a hint. A finding you accept on purpose, with a reason, is kept in the draft's waivers.json and is left out of the count.
studio.guide.terminal.title: In the terminal
studio.guide.terminal.global: There is no global kitvas command. The normal way to run one is to ask Claude in plain words: "open the studio", "check the pricing draft". By hand, run this from your project folder:
studio.guide.terminal.folder: An installed plugin's folder is ~/.claude/plugins/cache/<marketplace>/kitvas/<version>/. This works after the first session. These are the commands you may run yourself:
studio.guide.command.status: Shows the version, settings and workspace.
studio.guide.command.studio: Starts the project's studio and prints its address. Also studio status and studio stop.
studio.guide.command.doctor: Checks the setup and says what is wrong.
studio.guide.command.draft: Creates, lists and shows drafts, starts a new version. Also delete, restore and purge.
studio.guide.command.kit: Lists, shows, checks, learns, verifies and selects kits.
studio.guide.command.browser: Shows the browser the checks use. browser install downloads Chromium.
studio.guide.trouble.title: When something does not work
studio.guide.trouble.line: Run kitvas doctor. It checks the setup and says what to do for each check that is not ok. It changes nothing that lasts.
studio.shortcuts.title: Shortcuts
studio.doctor.title: Doctor
studio.doctor.lead: What kitvas found when it checked the setup. Nothing it does here changes anything that lasts.
studio.doctor.reportNote: Nothing private is in it: your home folder is written as ~ and the project folder as <project>, and names and addresses are left out. Paste it into an issue.
studio.doctor.unavailable: The doctor could not run here.
studio.doctor.byHand: Run these from your project folder in a terminal. The second one prints the report to paste into an issue.
